title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Compensation for Personal Injury in Railway Transport

articles.content_en:
Article 1. This Interpretation shall apply to the People's Courts' trial of disputes over compensation for personal injury in railway transport caused by railway traffic accidents and other railway operation accidents.
Disputes over compensation for personal injury caused by railway transport enterprises to passengers during the performance of passenger transport contracts shall not be governed by this Interpretation; personal injury suffered by railway workers who have established labor contract relations or formed labor relations with railway transport enterprises in the performance of their duties shall be handled in accordance with the legal provisions regulating labor relations and other relevant legal provisions.
Article 2. The victim of personal injury in railway transport and the close relatives of a deceased victim shall be the compensation right holders and shall have the right to claim compensation.

Article 3. Where a compensation right holder requests the other party to bear tort liability, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the railway transport court at the place where the accident occurred, the place where the train first arrived, or the place where the defendant is domiciled.
Where the area specified in the preceding paragraph has no railway transport court, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of another People's Court designated by the Higher People's Court.
Article 4. Where railway transport causes personal injury, the railway transport enterprise shall bear compensation liability; where laws provide otherwise, those laws shall prevail.

Article 6. Where personal injury is caused by the victim's wrongful act, and the railway transport enterprise shall bear compensation liability according to law, the compensation liability of the railway transport enterprise may be appropriately reduced according to the degree of the victim's fault, and shall be handled separately in accordance with the following circumstances:
(1) Where the railway transport enterprise fails to fully perform its obligations such as safety protection and warning, and bears primary liability for the accident, it shall bear compensation liability between 90% and 60% of the total damage; where the railway transport enterprise bears equal liability for the accident, it shall bear compensation liability between 60% and 50% of the total damage; where the railway transport enterprise bears secondary liability for the accident, it shall bear compensation liability between 40% and 10% of the total damage;
(2) Where the railway transport enterprise has fully performed its obligations such as safety protection and warning, but the victim still commits a wrongful act, the railway transport enterprise shall bear compensation liability within 10% of the total damage.
Where the railway transport enterprise has fully performed its obligations such as safety protection and warning, and the victim, disregarding the dissuasion of the personnel on duty, forcibly crosses a railway level crossing or pedestrian passage, or, knowing the dangerous consequences, still ignores the warning rules and walks longitudinally along railway lines, sits or lies down, intentionally causing personal injury, the railway transport enterprise shall not bear compensation liability, unless there is evidence proving that the injury was not intentionally caused by the victim.

Article 7. Where railway transport causes personal injury to a person who has no capacity for civil conduct, the railway transport enterprise shall bear compensation liability; if the guardian is at fault, the compensation liability of the railway transport enterprise shall be reduced according to the degree of fault.
Where railway transport causes personal injury to a person with limited capacity for civil conduct, the railway transport enterprise shall bear compensation liability; if the guardian or the victim himself is at fault, the compensation liability of the railway transport enterprise shall be reduced according to the degree of fault.

Article 8. Where a collision between railway rolling stock and a motor vehicle causes personal injury to a person other than the motor vehicle driver, the railway transport enterprise and the motor vehicle party shall bear joint and several compensation liability to the victim. The share of liability between the railway transport enterprise and the motor vehicle party shall be determined according to the respective degrees of liability; where it is difficult to determine the degrees of liability, they shall bear liability equally. A party that has actually borne compensation liability to the victim in excess of its due share shall have the right to claim recourse against the other party.
Where a collision between railway rolling stock and a motor vehicle causes personal injury to the motor vehicle driver, the provisions of Articles 4 to 6 of this Interpretation shall apply.

Article 9. Where an accident occurs at an unattended railway crossing that is not under the guardianship of a railway transport enterprise and causes personal injury, the railway transport enterprise shall bear compensation liability in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Interpretation. If the crossing management unit is at fault, the railway transport enterprise, after bearing compensation liability to the compensation right holder, shall have the right to claim recourse against the crossing management unit.

Article 10. Where a unit responsible for the management, maintenance, and other duties of railway bridges, culverts, and other facilities fails to perform its duties, rendering such railway bridges, culverts, and other facilities unable to be used normally, and thereby causing personal injury to pedestrians or vehicles crossing railway lines, the railway transport enterprise, after bearing compensation liability in accordance with the relevant provisions of this Interpretation, shall have the right to claim recourse against that unit.

Article 11. An accident determination document produced by an organization authorized to make accident determinations in accordance with the Regulations on Emergency Rescue, Investigation and Handling of Railway Traffic Accidents and other relevant provisions, after being cross-examined in court, shall be used by the People's Court as the basis for ascertaining facts provided that the parties have no sufficient contrary evidence and reasons to overturn the facts determined therein.

Article 12. Where personal injury is caused by transport on special railways and railway special lines, and according to law the owner, user, or manager of the tool or equipment causing the accident shall bear compensation liability, this Interpretation shall apply.
Article 13. Where any judicial interpretation previously issued by this Court is inconsistent with this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall prevail.
